audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the P2P gossip validation layer validate commitment_indices bounds before passing to verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: The Go implementation does not have a 'commitment_indices' array in the sense implied by the checklist item. sidecar.Index (the column index, range 0-127) is used as the cell_index. VerifyDataColumnSidecar at p2p_interface.go:36-38 checks sidecar.Index >= numberOfColumns (128) and returns ErrIndexTooLarge before KZG verification. This guard fires in ValidFields() at the topmost P2P validation layer before the sidecar ever reaches VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs.
phase1.data_flow: P2P -> decodePubsubMessage -> NewRODataColumn -> validateDataColumn -> verifier.ValidFields() -> VerifyDataColumnSidecar [INDEX CHECK HERE] -> validateWithKzgBatchVerifier -> verifyKzgBatch -> VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs -> kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch -> ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch (C)
invariants_checked: SSZ-typed arrays prevent incorrect sizes at deserialization

phase2.symbolic_execution: Symbolic path: attacker sends sidecar.Index = 128 (= NumberOfColumns). VerifyDataColumnSidecar returns ErrIndexTooLarge. ValidFields() returns that error. validateDataColumn returns pubsub.ValidationReject. KZG verification never reached. The C library also independently checks cell_indices[i] >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB (128) returning C_KZG_BADARGS - defense in depth.
attack_scenarios_tested: cell_index = CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB (128) -> rejected at Go layer
cell_index = MAX_UINT64 -> rejected at Go layer (>= 128)
Multiple sidecars with mixed valid/invalid indices -> each validated independently

phase2_5.guard_sufficiency: The guard sidecar.Index >= numberOfColumns is tight: numberOfColumns = CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB = 128. The Go guard precisely matches the C precondition. No gap exists between what Go validates and what C requires.
phase2_5.bypass_attempts: No bypass found. The check occurs at ValidFields() before the sidecar enters any processing pipeline.

phase3.invariant_proving: PROVED: For all P2P-received sidecars, sidecar.Index < 128 is established before VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs is called. The C library receives only valid cell indices.

phase3_5.adversarial_review: No exploitation path found. The guard is at the correct location (before KZG dispatch), checks the correct condition (exact match with C library precondition), and is not bypassable via SSZ deserialization.

audit_items.reasoning: VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks sidecar.Index >= NumberOfColumns (128) and rejects before any KZG operation. NumberOfColumns equals CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB exactly. Defense-in-depth: the C library also performs its own bounds check. No out-of-bounds commitment_indices access possible from P2P input.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does P2P gossip validation layer reject data column sidecars with cell_index >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB before reaching verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: While the P2P layer correctly rejects cell_index >= 128, a critical goroutine deadlock was identified in validateWithKzgBatchVerifier (batch_verifier.go:163). The function creates an unbuffered channel `resChan := make(chan error)`, sends a verificationSet to kzgChan, then waits with a context timeout (SecondsPerSlot = 12s). If the timeout fires before verifyKzgBatch sends the result, validateWithKzgBatchVerifier returns ValidationIgnore and abandons the unbuffered channel. verifyKzgBatch later attempts `verifier.resChan <- verificationErr` with no reader - this blocks forever. The kzgVerifierRoutine goroutine is permanently deadlocked.
invariants_checked: Unbuffered channel with context timeout pattern

phase2.symbolic_execution: Deadlock scenario: T0: validateWithKzgBatchVerifier creates unbuffered resChan at line 163, sends to kzgChan. T1: context timeout fires (12s elapsed - possible under load). T2: validateWithKzgBatchVerifier returns ValidationIgnore, abandons resChan. T3: kzgVerifierRoutine's verifyKzgBatch calls VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs (may take seconds for large batch). T4: verifyKzgBatch attempts `verifier.resChan <- verificationErr` - BLOCKS FOREVER (unbuffered, no reader). T5: kzgVerifierRoutine permanently blocked in verifyKzgBatch. T6: Subsequent KZG requests block on `s.kzgChan <- verificationSet` once kzgChan fills. T7: All P2P gossip validation for data column sidecars stalls. T8: Node cannot process any data column sidecars until restart.
attack_scenarios_tested: High-load: many sidecars arrive simultaneously, batch takes >12s -> organic deadlock
Attacker floods with large valid sidecars to delay batch processing beyond timeout
Network reconnect with many missed sidecars triggers large batch exceeding timeout
phase2.counterexample: CONFIRMED: Deadlock is reproducible whenever batch KZG verification exceeds SecondsPerSlot (12s on mainnet). Triggerable organically under load or via deliberate amplification.

phase2_5.guard_sufficiency: The cell_index check is correct. However, this analysis reveals a separate critical vulnerability in channel management. The guard does not prevent the deadlock.
phase2_5.exploit_details: Root cause: `resChan := make(chan error)` at batch_verifier.go:163. Fix: `make(chan error, 1)`. The 1-buffer allows verifyKzgBatch to always complete its send without blocking even when receiver has timed out.
phase2_5.attack_feasibility: High. Triggerable under network load. No special permissions - any P2P peer can participate. Once triggered, permanently stalls KZG verification pipeline.
phase2_5.bypass_attempts: No recovery mechanism exists once deadlock occurs. validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg is only called when resChan delivers an error, but verifyKzgBatch is blocked so no error is ever delivered.

phase3.invariant_proving: VIOLATED: Liveness invariant 'kzgVerifierRoutine always processes pending verifications' violated when context timeout occurs before verifyKzgBatch completes. Unbuffered channel creates permanent goroutine leak and pipeline stall.
phase3.formal_verdict: VULNERABILITY - Goroutine deadlock causing permanent KZG verification pipeline stall

phase3_5.adversarial_review: Confirmed high-severity vulnerability. Fix is trivial (buffered channel) but impact is severe: permanent DoS of data column sidecar processing. Node cannot recover without restart.
phase3_5.severity_assessment: High. Permanent DoS of KZG verification pipeline. No crash but node cannot process PeerDAS data columns.

vulnerability_details.title: Unbuffered resChan in validateWithKzgBatchVerifier causes permanent goroutine deadlock
vulnerability_details.impact: Permanent stall of kzgVerifierRoutine goroutine when context timeout fires before verifyKzgBatch completes. Cascades to stalling all P2P data column sidecar KZG verification. Node requires restart to recover.
exploit_chain: 1. P2P data column sidecars arrive under high load or attacker floods network
2. verifyKzgBatch takes longer than SecondsPerSlot (12s) to process large accumulated batch
3. validateWithKzgBatchVerifier context timeout fires, returns ValidationIgnore
5. verifyKzgBatch blocks permanently on resChan <- verificationErr
7. kzgChan fills up, all subsequent s.kzgChan <- sends block
8. All P2P gossip validation for data column sidecars stalls
9. Node cannot participate in PeerDAS data availability sampling

Fix: `make(chan error, 1)`. Impact: permanent stall of KZG verification pipeline requiring node restart.

phase3.invariant_proving: PROVED for byte length and KZG soundness. CHK-0109 deadlock vulnerability applies when cells used to amplify batch processing time.
phase3.formal_verdict: VULNERABILITY (references CHK-0109 deadlock as primary finding)

phase3_5.adversarial_review: Direct concern not a vulnerability. CHK-0109 deadlock is the actual exploitable vulnerability reachable via this attack surface.

vulnerability_details.title: Unbuffered resChan deadlock (CHK-0109) - reachable via cell flooding
vulnerability_details.note: The direct concern (incorrect cell bytes) is not vulnerable. SSZ enforces sizes; KZG ensures soundness. However, the CHK-0109 unbuffered channel deadlock is exploitable via this attack surface (flooding valid sidecars).

audit_items.reasoning: Direct concern (incorrect cell length causing wrong verification) is not a vulnerability. The CHK-0109 unbuffered channel deadlock at batch_verifier.go:163 is the critical finding, reachable via this attack surface. Fix: `make(chan error, 1)`.
